sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca pravartamāne dyūte tu matsyaḥ pāṇḍavam abravīt paśya putreṇa me yuddhe tādṛśāḥ kuravo jitāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: While the game of dice was in progress, Matsya said to the Pāṇḍava: 'See — such Kurus as these have been defeated in battle by my son.'

sanskrit: tato 'bravīn matsyarājaṃ dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ bṛhannaḍā yasya yantā kathaṃ sa na vijeṣyati
english: Then Dharmaputra Yudhiṣṭhira said to the king of Matsya: 'He whose charioteer is Bṛhannaḍā — how could he not be victorious?'

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ kupito rājā matsyaḥ pāṇḍavam abravīt samaṃ putreṇa me ṣaṇḍhaṃ brahmabandho praśaṃsasi
english: At these words king Matsya grew angry and said to the Pāṇḍava: 'You equate a eunuch with my son and praise him — you wretch of a brahmin!'

sanskrit: vācyāvācyaṃ na jānīṣe nūnaṃ mām avamanyase bhīṣmadroṇamukhān sarvān kasmān na sa vijeṣyati
english: 'You do not know what should and should not be said; surely you hold me in contempt. Why would he not conquer them all — Bhīṣma, Droṇa, and the rest?'

sanskrit: vayasyatvāt tu te brahmann aparādham imaṃ kṣame nedṛśaṃ te punar vācyaṃ yadi jīvitum icchasi
english: 'Out of friendship I forgive this offence of yours, brahmin — but such a thing must not be spoken again by you, if you wish to live.'

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca yatra droṇas tathā bhīṣmo drauṇir vaikartanaḥ kṛpaḥ duryodhanaś ca rājendra tathānye ca mahārathāḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: 'Where Droṇa, Bhīṣma, Drauṇi, Karṇa the son of Vikartana, Kṛpa, Duryodhana, and other great warriors stand together, O king —'

sanskrit: marudgaṇaiḥ parivṛtaḥ sākṣād api śatakratuḥ ko 'nyo bṛhannaḍāyās tān pratiyudhyeta saṃgatān
english: '— even Indra of a hundred sacrifices, surrounded by the hosts of Maruts, could scarcely face them in array. Who else but Bṛhannaḍā could oppose them when united?'

sanskrit: virāṭa uvāca bahuśaḥ pratiṣiddho 'si na ca vācaṃ niyacchasi niyantā cen na vidyeta na kaś cid dharmam ācaret
english: Virāṭa said: 'You have been restrained many times, yet you do not check your tongue. If there were no one to restrain, no one would observe dharma.'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ prakupito rājā tam akṣeṇāhanad bhṛśam mukhe yudhiṣṭhiraṃ kopān naivam ity eva bhartsayan
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the king, inflamed with rage, struck Yudhiṣṭhira hard on the face with a dice, chiding him in anger: 'Not so!'

sanskrit: balavat pratividdhasya nastaḥ śoṇitam āgamat tad aprāptaṃ mahīṃ pārthaḥ pāṇibhyāṃ pratyagṛhṇata
english: Struck with great force, blood flowed from his nose; before it could reach the ground, the son of Pṛthā caught it in his cupped hands.

sanskrit: avaikṣata ca dharmātmā draupadīṃ pārśvataḥ sthitām sā veda tam abhiprāyaṃ bhartuś cittavaśānugā
english: The righteous-souled one glanced at Draupadī standing nearby; she, who always followed her husband's thoughts, understood his intention.

sanskrit: pūrayitvā ca sauvarṇaṃ pātraṃ kāṃsyam aninditā tac choṇitaṃ pratyagṛhṇād yat prasusrāva pāṇḍavāt
english: The blameless one filled a golden bronze vessel and received in it the blood that had flowed from the Pāṇḍava, letting not a drop fall.

sanskrit: athottaraḥ śubhair gandhair mālyaiś ca vividhais tathā avakīryamāṇaḥ saṃhṛṣṭo nagaraṃ svairam āgamat
english: Meanwhile Uttara, showered with sweet fragrant garlands and flowers of many kinds, came joyfully at his ease into the city.

sanskrit: sabhājyamānaḥ pauraiś ca strībhir jānapadais tathā āsādya bhavanadvāraṃ pitre sa pratyahārayat
english: Honoured by the citizens, by women, and by country folk, he reached the gate of the palace and presented himself before his father.

sanskrit: tato dvāḥsthaḥ praviśyaiva virāṭam idam abravīt bṛhannaḍāsahāyas te putro dvāry uttaraḥ sthitaḥ
english: Then a door-keeper entered and reported to Virāṭa: 'Your son Uttara stands at the gate, accompanied by Bṛhannaḍā.'

sanskrit: tato hṛṣṭo matsyarājaḥ kṣattāram idam abravīt praveśyatām ubhau tūrṇaṃ darśanepsur ahaṃ tayoḥ
english: Then the delighted king of Matsya said to his chamberlain: 'Let both of them be brought in at once — I am eager to see them.'

sanskrit: kṣattāraṃ kururājas tu śanaiḥ karṇa upājapat uttaraḥ praviśatv eko na praveśyā bṛhannaḍā
english: But the Kuru king — Yudhiṣṭhira — whispered softly to the chamberlain: 'Let Uttara enter alone; Bṛhannaḍā is not to be admitted.'

sanskrit: etasya hi mahābāho vratam etat samāhitam yo mamāṅge vraṇaṃ kuryāc choṇitaṃ vāpi darśayet anyatra saṃgrāmagatān na sa jīved asaṃśayam
english: 'For this mighty-armed one has taken this firm vow: whoever makes a wound on his body or causes blood to appear — except on the field of battle — shall not live, without doubt.'

sanskrit: na mṛṣyād bhṛśasaṃkruddho māṃ dṛṣṭvaiva saśoṇitam virāṭam iha sāmātyaṃ hanyāt sabalavāhanam
english: 'Seeing me with blood on my face, he would not endure it in his fierce anger — he would slay Virāṭa here along with his ministers, troops, and vehicles.'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato rājñaḥ suto jyeṣṭhaḥ prāviśat pṛthivīṃjayaḥ so 'bhivādya pituḥ pādau dharmarājam apaśyata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then the king's eldest son, Pṛthivīṃjaya, entered; having saluted his father's feet, he noticed Dharmarāja.

sanskrit: sa taṃ rudhirasaṃsiktam anekāgram anāgasam bhūmāv āsīnam ekānte sairandhryā samupasthitam
english: He saw him seated apart on the ground, spattered with blood, his mind deeply concentrated, innocent of any offence, attended by the Sairandhrī.

sanskrit: tataḥ papraccha pitaraṃ tvaramāṇa ivottaraḥ kenāyaṃ tāḍito rājan kena pāpam idaṃ kṛtam
english: Then Uttara hastily questioned his father: 'By whom has this man been struck, O king? Who has committed this evil deed?'

sanskrit: virāṭa uvāca mayāyaṃ tāḍito jihmo na cāpy etāvad arhati praśasyamāne yaḥ śūre tvayi ṣaṇḍhaṃ praśaṃsati
english: Virāṭa said: 'This crooked one was struck by me, and he deserved even more than that — one who praises a eunuch when a hero like you is being praised.'

sanskrit: uttara uvāca akāryaṃ te kṛtaṃ rājan kṣipram eva prasādyatām mā tvā brahmaviṣaṃ ghoraṃ samūlam api nirdahet
english: Uttara said: 'You have done what should not be done, O king — appease him at once. Let the terrible poison of a brahmin's curse not burn you up, roots and all.'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca sa putrasya vacaḥ śrutvā virāṭo rāṣṭravardhanaḥ kṣamayām āsa kaunteyaṃ bhasmacchannam ivānalam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Hearing his son's words, Virāṭa, that enlarger of his kingdom, sought forgiveness from the son of Kuntī — as one would seek to placate a fire covered with ashes.

sanskrit: kṣamayantaṃ tu rājānaṃ pāṇḍavaḥ pratyabhāṣata ciraṃ kṣāntam idaṃ rājan na manyur vidyate mama
english: The Pāṇḍava replied to the king who was seeking forgiveness: 'I have long since forgiven it, O king; there is no anger in me.'

sanskrit: yadi hy etat pated bhūmau rudhiraṃ mama nastataḥ sarāṣṭras tvaṃ mahārāja vinaśyethā na saṃśayaḥ
english: 'For if this blood from my nose had fallen on the ground, you, great king, together with your whole kingdom, would surely have been destroyed — there is no doubt.'

sanskrit: na dūṣayāmi te rājan yac ca hanyād adūṣakam balavantaṃ mahārāja kṣipraṃ dāruṇam āpnuyāt
english: 'I do not blame you, O king. But one who strikes an innocent man will quickly meet a terrible fate, great king.'

sanskrit: śoṇite tu vyatikrānte praviveśa bṛhannaḍā abhivādya virāṭaṃ ca kaṅkaṃ cāpy upatiṣṭhata
english: Once the blood had been dealt with, Bṛhannaḍā entered, saluted Virāṭa, and attended upon Kaṅka as well.

sanskrit: kṣamayitvā tu kauravyaṃ raṇād uttaram āgatam praśaśaṃsa tato matsyaḥ śṛṇvataḥ savyasācinaḥ
english: Having reconciled with the Kauravya, Matsya then praised Uttara — who had come back from battle — within the hearing of Savyasācin.

sanskrit: tvayā dāyādavān asmi kaikeyīnandivardhana tvayā me sadṛśaḥ putro na bhūto na bhaviṣyati
english: 'Through you I have an heir, O joy and glory of the Kaikeyīs. A son equal to you has not existed before me nor shall exist hereafter.'

sanskrit: padaṃ padasahasreṇa yaś caran nāparādhnuyāt tena karṇena te tāta katham āsīt samāgamaḥ
english: 'He who strides a thousand paces and never errs — how was your encounter with that Karṇa, my child?'

sanskrit: manuṣyaloke sakale yasya tulyo na vidyate yaḥ samudra ivākṣobhyaḥ kālāgnir iva duḥsahaḥ tena bhīṣmeṇa te tāta katham āsīt samāgamaḥ
english: 'He who has no equal in all the world of men, who is as unshakeable as the ocean and as unbearable as the fire of destruction — how was your encounter with that Bhīṣma, my child?'

sanskrit: ācāryo vṛṣṇivīrāṇāṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ ca yo dvijaḥ sarvakṣatrasya cācāryaḥ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varaḥ tena droṇena te tāta katham āsīt samāgamaḥ
english: 'He who is the preceptor of the Vṛṣṇi heroes and of the Pāṇḍavas, the teacher of all the kṣatriyas, the foremost of all who bear weapons — how was your encounter with that Droṇa, my child?'

sanskrit: ācāryaputro yaḥ śūraḥ sarvaśastrabhṛtām api aśvatthāmeti vikhyātaḥ kathaṃ tena samāgamaḥ
english: 'The son of the preceptor who is the hero famed above all bearers of weapons, known as Aśvatthāmā — how was your encounter with him?'

sanskrit: raṇe yaṃ prekṣya sīdanti hṛtasvā vaṇijo yathā kṛpeṇa tena te tāta katham āsīt samāgamaḥ
english: 'He at whose sight in battle men quail like merchants who have lost their wealth — how was your encounter with that Kṛpa, my child?'

sanskrit: parvataṃ yo 'bhividhyeta rājaputro maheṣubhiḥ duryodhanena te tāta katham āsīt samāgamaḥ
english: 'The royal prince who could pierce a mountain with his mighty arrows — how was your encounter with that Duryodhana, my child?'

sanskrit: uttara uvāca na mayā nirjitā gāvo na mayā nirjitāḥ pare kṛtaṃ tu karma tat sarvaṃ devaputreṇa kena cit
english: Uttara said: 'It was not I who won back the cattle, nor I who defeated the enemy. All that was accomplished by a certain son of a god.'

sanskrit: sa hi bhītaṃ dravantaṃ māṃ devaputro nyavārayat sa cātiṣṭhad rathopasthe vajrahastanibho yuvā
english: 'For when I was frightened and fleeing, that son of a god stopped me; the young man, resembling Indra the thunderbolt-holder, stood in the rear of the chariot.'

sanskrit: tena tā nirjitā gāvas tena te kuravo jitāḥ tasya tat karma vīrasya na mayā tāta tat kṛtam
english: 'By him were the cattle won back; by him were those Kurus defeated. That deed belongs to that hero — it was not done by me, father.'

sanskrit: sa hi śāradvataṃ droṇaṃ droṇaputraṃ ca vīryavān sūtaputraṃ ca bhīṣmaṃ ca cakāra vimukhāñ śaraiḥ
english: 'That mighty one turned back with his arrows Śāradvatī's son Kṛpa, Droṇa, Droṇa's son, the son of a sūta, and Bhīṣma.'

sanskrit: duryodhanaṃ ca samare sanāgam iva yūthapam prabhagnam abravīd bhītaṃ rājaputraṃ mahābalam
english: 'And in battle he rebuked Duryodhana, the mighty prince, who was broken like a bull-elephant driven from the herd, trembling with fear.'

sanskrit: na hāstinapure trāṇaṃ tava paśyāmi kiṃ cana vyāyāmena parīpsasva jīvitaṃ kauravātmaja
english: '"I see no refuge for you in Hāstinapura; strive with all effort to save your life, son of the Kurus."'

sanskrit: na mokṣyase palāyaṃs tvaṃ rājan yuddhe manaḥ kuru pṛthivīṃ bhokṣyase jitvā hato vā svargam āpsyasi
english: '"You will not escape by fleeing, O king; set your mind on battle — conquer and you shall enjoy the earth, or fall and you shall attain heaven."'

sanskrit: sa nivṛtto naravyāghro muñcan vajranibhāñ śarān sacivaiḥ saṃvṛto rājā rathe nāga iva śvasan
english: 'Then that tiger among men turned back, releasing arrows like thunderbolts, the king surrounded by his ministers, panting in his chariot like an elephant.'

sanskrit: tatra me romaharṣo 'bhūd ūrustambhaś ca māriṣa yad abhraghanasaṃkāśam anīkaṃ vyadhamac charaiḥ
english: 'There my hair stood on end and my thighs became rigid, O worthy one, as he shattered that army — dark as a mass of thunder-clouds — with his arrows.'

sanskrit: tat praṇudya rathānīkaṃ siṃhasaṃhanano yuvā kurūṃs tān prahasan rājan vāsāṃsy apaharad balī
english: 'Repelling the force of chariots, that lion-built youth laughed at those Kurus, O king, and the powerful one stripped them of their garments.'

sanskrit: ekena tena vīreṇa ṣaḍrathāḥ parivāritāḥ śārdūleneva mattena mṛgās tṛṇacarā vane
english: 'By that single hero, six warriors in their chariots were surrounded — like deer grazing in the forest surrounded by a maddened tiger.'

sanskrit: virāṭa uvāca kva sa vīro mahābāhur devaputro mahāyaśāḥ yo me dhanam avājaiṣīt kurubhir grastam āhave
english: Virāṭa said: 'Where is that mighty-armed hero, the son of a god, of great renown, who won back my wealth seized by the Kurus in battle?'

sanskrit: icchāmi tam ahaṃ draṣṭum arcituṃ ca mahābalam yena me tvaṃ ca gāvaś ca rakṣitā devasūnunā
english: 'I wish to see and honour that mighty one by whose — that divine son's — power both you and my cattle were protected.'

sanskrit: uttara uvāca antardhānaṃ gatas tāta devaputraḥ pratāpavān sa tu śvo vā paraśvo vā manye prādurbhaviṣyati
english: Uttara said: 'That glorious son of a god has vanished from sight, father; but I think he will reappear tomorrow or the day after.'

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam ākhyāyamānaṃ tu channaṃ satreṇa pāṇḍavam vasantaṃ tatra nājñāsīd virāṭaḥ pārtham arjunam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Even as this account was being given, Virāṭa did not recognise the Pāṇḍava — Pārtha Arjuna — who was dwelling there concealed by his guise.

sanskrit: tataḥ pārtho 'bhyanujñāto virāṭena mahātmanā pradadau tāni vāsāṃsi virāṭaduhituḥ svayam
english: Then Pārtha, having obtained the permission of the great-souled Virāṭa, himself gave those garments to Virāṭa's daughter.

sanskrit: uttarā tu mahārhāṇi vividhāni tanūni ca pratigṛhyābhavat prītā tāni vāsāṃsi bhāminī
english: And Uttarā, the spirited princess, accepted those garments — precious and of many kinds and delicate — and was pleased.

sanskrit: mantrayitvā tu kaunteya uttareṇa rahas tadā itikartavyatāṃ sarvāṃ rājany atha yudhiṣṭhire
english: Then the son of Kuntī privately counselled with Uttara about everything that needed to be done — the entire course of action — regarding king Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: tatas tathā tad vyadadhād yathāvat puruṣarṣabha saha putreṇa matsyasya prahṛṣṭo bharatarṣabhaḥ
english: And so the bull among men, bull among Bharatas, duly arranged all of that, joyful, together with the son of Matsya.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tatas tṛtīye divase bhrātaraḥ pañca pāṇḍavāḥ snātāḥ śuklāmbaradharāḥ samaye caritavratāḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: On the third day thereafter, the five Pāṇḍava brothers, bathed, clad in white garments, having fulfilled the vow that was theirs to keep —

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiraṃ puraskṛtya sarvābharaṇabhūṣitāḥ abhipadmā yathā nāgā bhrājamānā mahārathāḥ
english: — with Yudhiṣṭhira at their head, adorned with all their ornaments, like great bull-elephants in full array, those great warriors shining resplendent —

sanskrit: virāṭasya sabhāṃ gatvā bhūmipālāsaneṣv atha niṣeduḥ pāvakaprakhyāḥ sarve dhiṣṇyeṣv ivāgnayaḥ
english: — entered the assembly hall of Virāṭa and there sat down upon the seats of rulers — all of them blazing like fire, like sacred fires upon their hearths.

sanskrit: teṣu tatropaviṣṭeṣu virāṭaḥ pṛthivīpatiḥ ājagāma sabhāṃ kartuṃ rājakāryāṇi sarvaśaḥ
english: While they were seated there, Virāṭa, the lord of the earth, came to the assembly hall to attend to all the affairs of state.

sanskrit: śrīmataḥ pāṇḍavān dṛṣṭvā jvalataḥ pāvakān iva atha matsyo 'bravīt kaṅkaṃ devarūpam avasthitam marudgaṇair upāsīnaṃ tridaśānām iveśvaram
english: Seeing the glorious Pāṇḍavas blazing like fires, Matsya said to Kaṅka — who sat there in godlike bearing, attended by them like the lord of the thirty gods attended by the Marut hosts:

sanskrit: sa kilākṣātivāpas tvaṃ sabhāstāro mayā kṛtaḥ atha rājāsane kasmād upaviṣṭo 'sy alaṃkṛtaḥ
english: 'You are said to be merely a dice-player whom I made a floor-scrubber of the assembly; why then do you sit adorned upon a royal seat?'

sanskrit: parihāsepsayā vākyaṃ virāṭasya niśamya tat smayamāno 'rjuno rājann idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Hearing that mocking remark of Virāṭa, Arjuna, smiling, spoke these words, O king:

sanskrit: indrasyāpy āsanaṃ rājann ayam āroḍhum arhati brahmaṇyaḥ śrutavāṃs tyāgī yajñaśīlo dṛḍhavrataḥ
english: 'Even Indra's seat, O king, is deserved by this man — devoted to brahmins, learned, generous, practised in sacrifice, firm in his vows.'

sanskrit: ayaṃ kurūṇām ṛṣabhaḥ kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ asya kīrtiḥ sthitā loke sūryasyevodyataḥ prabhā
english: 'This is the bull of the Kurus, Kuntī's son Yudhiṣṭhira; his fame stands in the world like the radiance of the risen sun.'

sanskrit: saṃsaranti diśaḥ sarvā yaśaso 'sya gabhastayaḥ uditasyeva sūryasya tejaso 'nu gabhastayaḥ
english: 'The rays of his glory course through all directions, just as the rays of the sun's radiance course when it has risen.'

sanskrit: enaṃ daśa sahasrāṇi kuñjarāṇāṃ tarasvinām anvayuḥ pṛṣṭhato rājan yāvad adhyāvasat kurūn
english: 'Ten thousand swift elephants followed behind him, O king, for as long as he dwelt among the Kurus.'

sanskrit: triṃśad enaṃ sahasrāṇi rathāḥ kāñcanamālinaḥ sadaśvair upasaṃpannāḥ pṛṣṭhato 'nuyayuḥ sadā
english: 'Thirty thousand chariots wreathed in gold, furnished with excellent horses, always followed behind him.'

sanskrit: enam aṣṭaśatāḥ sūtāḥ sumṛṣṭamaṇikuṇḍalāḥ astuvan māgadhaiḥ sārdhaṃ purā śakram ivarṣayaḥ
english: 'Eight hundred bards, wearing finely polished jewelled earrings, used to sing his praises together with the Māgadha singers, as sages praise Indra.'

sanskrit: enaṃ nityam upāsanta kuravaḥ kiṃkarā yathā sarve ca rājan rājāno dhaneśvaram ivāmarāḥ
english: 'The Kurus waited upon him constantly as upon a master; all kings as well, O king, attended him as the immortals attend the lord of wealth.'

sanskrit: eṣa sarvān mahīpālān karam āhārayat tadā vaiśyān iva mahārāja vivaśān svavaśān api
english: 'This one exacted tribute from all the rulers of the earth at that time — even those who yielded of their own will and those who did not — as a lord exacts tribute from vaiśyas, great king.'

sanskrit: aṣṭāśītisahasrāṇi snātakānāṃ mahātmanām upajīvanti rājānam enaṃ sucaritavratam
english: 'Eighty-eight thousand great-souled snātakas lived by the patronage of this king, who was steadfast in his vows of good conduct.'

sanskrit: eṣa vṛddhān anāthāṃś ca vyaṅgān paṅgūṃś ca mānavān putravat pālayām āsa prajā dharmeṇa cābhibho
english: 'This one protected the aged, the helpless, the maimed, and the lame among men as if they were his own children, and governed his subjects by dharma, O overlord.'

sanskrit: eṣa dharme dame caiva krodhe cāpi yatavrataḥ mahāprasādo brahmaṇyaḥ satyavādī ca pārthivaḥ
english: 'This king is disciplined in dharma, in self-restraint, and even in anger; of great grace, devoted to brahmins, and ever truthful.'

sanskrit: śrīpratāpena caitasya tapyate sa suyodhanaḥ sagaṇaḥ saha karṇena saubalenāpi vā vibhuḥ
english: 'Suyodhana with his followers, along with Karṇa and the son of Subala — that mighty one — is scorched by his brilliance and majesty.'

sanskrit: na śakyante hy asya guṇāḥ prasaṃkhyātuṃ nareśvara eṣa dharmaparo nityam ānṛśaṃsyaś ca pāṇḍavaḥ
english: 'His virtues cannot be fully enumerated, O lord of men; this Pāṇḍava is ever devoted to dharma and ever free from cruelty.'

sanskrit: evaṃyukto mahārājaḥ pāṇḍavaḥ pārthivarṣabhaḥ kathaṃ nārhati rājārham āsanaṃ pṛthivīpatiḥ
english: 'Endowed with such qualities, this great king, this Pāṇḍava, this bull among kings, this lord of the earth — how is he unworthy of a royal seat?'

sanskrit: virāṭa uvāca yady eṣa rājā kauravyaḥ kuntīputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ katamo 'syārjuno bhrātā bhīmaś ca katamo balī
english: Virāṭa said: 'If this is king Yudhiṣṭhira, the Kauravya, son of Kuntī — then which of these is his brother Arjuna, and which is the mighty Bhīma?'

sanskrit: nakulaḥ sahadevo vā draupadī vā yaśasvinī yadā dyūte jitāḥ pārthā na prājñāyanta te kva cit
english: 'Where is Nakula, where Sahadeva, where the illustrious Draupadī? When the Pārthas were defeated at dice, they were nowhere to be found.'

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca ya eṣa ballavo brūte sūdas tava narādhipa eṣa bhīmo mahābāhur bhīmavegaparākramaḥ
english: Arjuna said: 'He who served as your cook and was called Ballava, O lord of men — that is Bhīma, the mighty-armed one, of terrible speed and valour.'
